profile.address: Ellis County, TX (Red Oak development campus, middle row)
profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record is one of eleven adjacent building footprints in Compass Datacenters Red Oak development, a wholesale data center campus in Ellis County, Texas, just south of the Dallas-Fort Worth core. This particular footprint sits in the middle row of the campus, the middle of three buildings arranged along that row, east of the campus westernmost cluster. Compass Datacenters own market materials describe this campus, part of its Dallas-Fort Worth market, as a 360 megawatt development that was still nearing completion as of the most recent site content reviewed, with a confirmed 200 million dollar expansion phase announced in April 2024 that added two buildings totaling more than 500,000 square feet. A separate July 2026 company news item states that Red Oak now hosts seven data centers total, though that figure appears to describe the city of Red Oak as a whole rather than Compass own building count specifically, so it should not be read as confirming exactly how many of the eleven OpenStreetMap footprints in this cluster are Compass-operated versus operated by other companies also active in the area. Compass Datacenters was founded in 2011 by Chris Crosby, a former Digital Realty senior executive who remains the company CEO, and completed its first data center, a 1.2 megawatt facility, in 2012. The company is headquartered in Dallas, Texas, and describes its current ownership, per its own about-us page, as Ontario Teachers Pension Plan, RedBird Capital Partners, and company management. Beyond Dallas-Fort Worth, Compass 2026 markets list includes active developments in Chicago Hoffman Estates, Northern Virginia Loudoun County, Toronto, and Milan, plus a newly broken-ground site in Meridian, Mississippi, alongside earlier markets including Minneapolis and Nashville that the company has since exited or transferred to independent ownership. Separately, Compass donated 12.6 million dollars to fund a 40,000 square foot workforce-training replica data center at 300 Houston School Road in Red Oak, operated by Texas State Technical College, a distinct facility from the wholesale buildings mapped here that should not be confused with them. No per-building capacity, square footage, tenant, or year-built figure could be confirmed for this specific structure within the campus, and no local government permit or tax-abatement record could be retrieved this session, so those figures are deliberately omitted rather than estimated from the campus-wide totals above.

reading.body:
Red Oak is a wholesale data center campus in Ellis County, Texas, south of Dallas-Fort Worth, operated by Compass Datacenters as part of a development described by the company as targeting 360 megawatts at full build-out. This particular building sits in the middle row of the campus, one of eleven mapped footprints in the locality, though the operator's confirmed capacity for this specific structure is not published. Compass announced a 200 million dollar expansion in April 2024 adding two buildings totaling more than 500,000 square feet, and the company remains in build-out phase as of the most recent available materials.

No confirmed megawatt figure, square footage, tenant identity, or completion date is published for this building. The campus overall has been variously described as targeting up to 350 to 360 megawatts, but no current or single-building figure attributable to this facility could be retrieved from operator spec pages or government records. At typical wholesale densities of 20 to 30 megawatts per building in a ten-building campus, the implied per-building average would be 36 to 54 megawatts, but this is calculation only and does not confirm actual capacity.

Compass Datacenters is owned by Ontario Teachers Pension Plan, RedBird Capital Partners, and company management, founded in 2011 by former Digital Realty executive Chris Crosby. The company operates active developments in Dallas-Fort Worth, Chicago, Northern Virginia, Toronto, Milan, and Mississippi, and has exited or transferred earlier markets including Minneapolis and Nashville. Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities with only 18 publishing confirmed megawatt figures totaling 468 megawatts, so Red Oak's lack of published capacity is common in the state and does not distinguish it.
